legend.title: How to read this forecast
legend.temperatureText: White: deep frost below {deepFrost}. Gray: frost up to {freezing}. Blue: cold up to {mild}. Green: comfortable up to {warm}. Orange: hot up to {hot}. Red: extreme heat above {hot}.
legend.feelsText: The shaded area shows how different the weather feels: blue below means it feels colder, while orange above means it feels warmer. The colored line is measured temperature and serves as the reference.
legend.skyText: Yellow glow is exposed sunlight and fades as cloud cover grows. The gray band becomes larger with more cloud. A moon marks nighttime.
legend.precipitationText: Symbol size shows the amount. Opacity shows probability.
legend.stormText: Lightning appears on the temperature chart. A larger, brighter bolt means a more probable and stronger storm.
legend.windText: The streams use one color. Calm conditions are nearly straight and faded. As wind strengthens, the parallel bands become thicker, spread farther apart, and form waves with increasing amplitude; their ends taper as the wind rises or fades. A narrowing vertical funnel marks an explicitly forecast tornado. Optional arrows show direction together with speed in km/h.
